overall: Atlanta is running notably cooler than model expectations as of early afternoon, with the temperature stalled at 78.8°F since at least 13:00 ET and a velocity of +0.0°F/hr indicating no active warming. The morning warm-up was sluggish (73.4°F held from 07:00–09:00), and the afternoon surge has so far plateaued well short of model targets. The moderately elevated dewpoint (62.6°F) and a 10+ mph wind are likely acting as a combined brake on further surface heating.
forecast_obs_notes: All three models (ECMWF 82.8°F, HRRR 84.4°F, NBM 82.3°F) cluster 3.5–5.6°F above the current running max, a gap that would be large to close even with robust afternoon heating — and the zero velocity at 13:05 ET makes that recovery look increasingly unlikely. The HRRR is the most aggressive and appears most at risk of busting high; ECMWF and NBM are closer together and somewhat more credible given the trend, but still imply a significant acceleration that the observed data is not yet supporting.
max_temp_prediction: With only roughly 2–3 hours of peak heating remaining and temperatures stalled at 78.8°F, a climb to the full model-consensus range of 82–84°F would require an unusually sharp afternoon surge that the current momentum does not support. The most likely outcome is a modest additional gain of 1.5–3°F as the sun angle remains favorable through ~15:30–16:00 ET, putting the daily high in the low 80s. Confidence is moderate-low given the model-obs gap; the best single estimate is near 81.0°F, with meaningful downside risk toward 80°F if the stall persists and upside capped around 82–83°F if heating briefly resumes.
